author: A fable, as told to children on the riverbank
pages:
#The Clever Mudcrab

Once upon a time, on the bank of a cold grey river, there lived a mudcrab who wanted to be a merchant. Every day he watched the traders' boats float past, laden with silks and spices, and he clicked his claws with longing.

#His First Customer

One day a weary traveller sat down on a rock beside him. The mudcrab scuttled forward and said, in a voice like pebbles grinding, "Good day! What will you buy?"

The traveller was so astonished that he bought a smooth river stone for five gold coins before he understood what had happened.

#Business Grows

Word spread. Travellers came from miles around to buy stones, shells and bits of driftwood from the talking mudcrab. He charged outrageous prices and refused to haggle, and somehow everyone paid. They went home and told their friends, and their friends came too.

Soon the mudcrab had a pile of gold taller than himself. He slept on it every night and dreamed of opening a shop in the city.

#The Lesson

But one morning a band of skeevers came down the river, saw the gold, and carried it all away while the mudcrab was busy arguing with a customer about the price of a pebble.

The mudcrab learned two lessons that day. First: guard your treasure. Second: never argue with a customer when you could be counting your coins.

He became the most careful merchant on the river, and the most bad-tempered, and lived happily ever after, in a crabby sort of way.
